what: Hashes for the protected (do-not-edit) analysis scripts, deposited because two of them had no hash recorded anywhere in paper/.

DEFECT.finding: gen_slope_r60.py and gen_slope_tier2_r87.py are on the do-not-edit list, but neither their full sha256 nor its 12-character prefix occurs in any file under paper/. The guard 'stop and ask if the file's sha256 is in the registration' therefore CANNOT FIRE for these two: there is nothing to match against.
DEFECT.found_how: Searched every live script hash across the whole paper/ tree, excluding .bak_ files. Five of seven were found and matched; two returned zero files for both the full hash and the 12-character prefix.

SELF_CORRECTION.first_answer: 4 of 7 scripts appeared to have no recorded hash.
SELF_CORRECTION.corrected_answer: 2 of 7. The other two WERE recorded and DO match.
SELF_CORRECTION.mechanism: The first pass used a regex requiring the hash to appear within 200 characters of the filename on the same line. Several registrations record the hash and the filename further apart or on separate lines, so the regex missed them. The robust check searched for each LIVE hash across the whole tree regardless of surrounding text.
SELF_CORRECTION.why_recorded: A narrower true finding replacing a wider false one is the direction an audit should move, and the mechanism is worth showing because the same proximity assumption would misfire again on any similarly formatted record.
